It's been about 2 months since my last post here - and it's been a few busy months. Next to some sickness in the family, I found myself fostering a handful orphaned kittens. Sleepless nights, stress, and plenty of restlessness ensued.

In the meantime, we still managed to find time to head out in the forest where we encountered the white beings, which turned out to not be white at all. My previous posts regarding this are https://voat.co/v/FolkishAsatru/3335211 and https://voat.co/v/FolkishAsatru/3318106. Pinging @Othmar_Regin and @NorthernMan

Since our first visits to the forest, there's been some changes. Of which the biggest one is that these fairies are immensely powerful. More about this in a bit. While we started going out of curiosity (our job is strongly intertwined with the paranormal, and we want to get to the bottom of mysteries), there's certainly a heavy aspect of respect in the matter. If you're curious, going out "to see fairies because it'd be cool" is really a bad idea. Going out into the forest to give respect where it's due and make offerings in celebration of the beings present is the right thing.

On to the current state of events

We're welcomed in the forest. Which means that we do not feel uneasy, however from the moment we set foot on the main road inside the forest, there is movement along the treelines and we can feel we're being watched. These beings are telepathic, and when they feel we've stood around long enough, we'll get a very clear message that our coming has been appreciated, and the gifts have been accepted, but that it would be pleasant for all parties if we go home. The parting usually is with an audible statement that we are thankful for being allowed to come by and commune with the beings. The leaving is quiet, and at times we're being walked out of the forest.

Being afraid is something that's greedily abused. Really. They love playing around with people. The best way to deal with them is to accept that you are no match for them, remain utterly respectful, and be ready to be studied with nothing left to hide. They are intrusive and downright terrifying, and without a doubt not beings you want to upset. Be honest and be prepared for glimpses of beings that are beautiful, entrancing, and otherworldly mighty.

Don't come needing to see them. They don't like that much. The first times we went to the forest, they were showing glimpses of themselves and teasing us that we could not see them. Mysterious and at the same time clear enough about not wanting to catch stares. If you come to their place with the main goal being to leave gifts and enjoy nature, the outcome is a whole lot different. I've already mentioned in the previous post that one of the beings stood next to me as I hung ribbons in a tree. It's happened at later times that my partner saw "shining silver eyes" right next to me, watching me as I went about my business. They like sneaking up on me, and I guess they prefer it when I am unaware of them being immensely close. I can feel it when people get close to me, since there's some electricity in the air, like when you hold a moth? But with these beings... The entire forest feels intensely alive.

When we started coming with the idea of bringing gifts, and entirely open to the prospect of being studied and followed around, we started seeing more. Trees moving. Branches pulled, and leaves rustling without wind. The movements always happened in heavier foliage, and it was so very clear there was no wind, because branches and leaves just next to the moving ones, would remain still. The most impressive is seeing a fairy walk. Perhaps naming them dryads would be more fitting - they're truly spirits of the trees. Their bodies are human-like, but their skin is like that of a smooth tree. Their eyes can light up. They are covered in bark, leaves, and animal skins. Very beautiful, but it's unclear whether they truly are or if they plant the idea of their enchanting presence in your mind through their telepathy. They'll show their true, entire selves when you no longer come near to see them, but rather to show yourself as wanting to be part of the forest.

They're utterly terrifying. I'm not saying this to come off as a badass because look at me, I go out to see fairies. They're blunt in talking about themselves. They love the paper ribbons I hang in the trees. First they were shy about them, but on being sure it's paper and it dissolves without a trace, they love them. When I've finished hanging all the ribbons I have, without a fail, a strong breeze will rise. The ribbons will move one by one. Even if there's 4 on the same branch, you can clearly see that they are moved one by one. Wind doesn't do this. They are like the wind, and they can summon a storm.

The terrifying thing is not in them liking ribbons. The terrifying thing is in them being able to change what you see. They've proven this before, and worded it as "even when you look straight at us, you will only see us if we want you to". Having an invisible 7 foot tall fairy right next to you that knows how to play tricks on your mind, that's the terrifying part. We don't notice them until they allow for a fast glimpse, only for them to disappear right again. It's kind of a game by now, I'd say. But we're no longer as focused on wanting to see them. We come to the forest to enjoy nature and have a quiet talk, speaking with the fairies if they are interested too. The only thing they always have us be aware of, is footsteps. Sometimes pulling on hairs or patting us. There is always a strong display of their power, and they are blunt about being capable of having people go mad with illusions. As are they blunt about how we better not leave any mess in the forest. While stepping on small plants during hanging ribbons is an accepted happening, they are very clear about disliking endangering of parts of the forest. Interesting enough, taking special care in avoiding plants where possible, running into stinging nettles does not provoke the expected reaction of being stung.

The next times we're building up our offerings. They speak in desires, and food is brought up. Traditionally, people in the areas we're living in, would make sacrifices of ribbons, food and drink, and clothes items. We're playing safe by giving what's not harmful to nature. Cloth ribbons aren't healthy for deer to ingest, and plastic ones would lay on the earth like waste. We believe that when you desire to make an offering to fairies, that it is a good thing to stick to what has been accepted traditionally.

Another thing worth mentioning is that leaving the forest doesn't mean that you leave the fairies. It happens frequently that we have small beings in the house after having visited the forest. They are about the size of two hands, and shoot to an intense black before fading to invisibility. They're like small people, but can be a lot more chubby. Overall they're sweet looking and they seem to have taken a liking to hanging on the softer pieces of furniture. While they're quiet, you can hear them rustling at times. They are shy, but seem to react rather well to calm talking and being greeted. Them hanging around doesn't last long usually, at the longest it's half a week. It seems they are a different species than the tree fairies, with these being more of a shadow type of fairy.

To conclude - the fairies of traditional lore are really a thing. While I'm not sure if they're still as numerous as before, I can say that making offerings from the desire of seeing the fairies and their forest become strong is not a bad thing. Just be sure you are okay with having your thoughts be intruded upon, as well as seeing and hearing things that you are not familiar with. Above all, be respectful to those you visit.

I'll be logging in more frequently now that my kittens are growing up, and am open to answering any questions. Don't think I'll be updating these posts any further, since the meetings in the forests are us making an offering, speaking with the fairies, enjoying nature, listening to a fairy-made wind rushing through the trees, and then wishing each other pleasant days until the next meeting, as well as thanking for the meeting. Were something to happen that significantly changes things, perhaps some advice on how to get in touch with nature spirits, then I'll make sure to post an update.
